scope: Verify that every seed form is attested in the cited scholarly literature and record the limits of the current normalized reference renderer. This audit does not claim attestation-specific allograph reconstruction.

status_definitions.reading_verified: The form or sequence is explicitly present in the cited scholarly source.
status_definitions.context_verified: The archaeological, numismatic, onomastic or formulaic context is supported by the source.
status_definitions.semantics_disputed: The sequence is attested, but its grammatical or lexical interpretation remains disputed.
status_definitions.normalized_reference_only: The current graphic output uses a normalized signary reference rather than the exact allograph of the attestation.

findings: The cited study uses ildiŕda in its title and discussion.
The article also prints a dotted epigraphic sequence i.l.ti.ŕ.ta for one coin legend; the current di/da tokens are a dual-value normalization and must not be presented as a facsimile.
erder is explicitly analysed as a monetary value expression.
Its proposed value of one half is a scholarly hypothesis supported by context, not a universally secure lexical translation.
undikesken is used in the cited numismatic comparison.
Conventional publications may also preserve forms such as untikesken; IberoLab follows the spelling used in the cited study and records variants rather than silently merging them.
ars is used by the cited study as the mint or monetary comparator associated with a hemidrachm.
The entry must not imply that ars alone reproduces the complete legend of every cited specimen.
The Ca n'Oliver publication explicitly identifies the authorship or production formula as characterised by ekiar/egiar.
The exact grammatical value is not treated as fully settled.
egiar is explicitly presented together with ekiar as a documented formulaic variant.
The current renderer represents the conventional reading, not the exact ductus of a specific vessel.
The Caminreal research review treats likine as one of the central anthroponymic elements of the mosaic inscription.
The page renders an isolated scholarly form and does not reconstruct the complete mosaic inscription.
The 2025 publication gives the complete sequence taŕśabańar and isolates the owner's name taŕśabań.
The transcription ń is verified as part of the scholarly reading, but the current generic sign series does not provide a safely assignable ń SVG.
The updated Sinarcas study explicitly discusses baisetaś in the funerary text.
Its status as a personal name is supported, while the precise role of the named person within the syntactic analysis remains debated.
seltar is explicitly present in the Sinarcas analysis and is treated in the funerary context as referring to the tomb or monument.
IberoLab labels this as a contextual interpretation, not an unrestricted dictionary translation.
ebanen is explicitly discussed in the updated Sinarcas study.
Competing analyses treat it as a possible filiation marker or as a verbal form; no translation is assigned by IberoLab.
